Upload CSV / Excel

Columns match PrimeHome Buyers' own required + optional fields (both now required to send: Call recording link and Ping ID), plus Phone (used to find an existing lead to fill in) — the two fields deliberately left out of the agent's submission form and entered here instead, per PrimeHome Buyers' "Provider lead fields description". For both, paste a URL directly here, or leave blank and upload an actual file per-lead in Lead Reviewing instead — either way a URL is what's actually sent. A row whose phone matches an existing lead fills in that lead's details; a row with no match creates a brand-new lead (attributed to you as the importer) ready for review below.

A raw call-intake export (Timestamp / Seller Name / Phone Number / Property Address / Condition / Occupancy / Reason / Closing / Additional Notes / Call Recording, etc. — not this template's own headers) is auto-detected and converted on upload, no pre-processing needed. Conversion skips DNC-tagged and unreadable rows and leaves fields it has no real signal for blank rather than guessing — the preview below always shows exactly what will be imported before anything is saved.

Task categories

Each category sets how idle detection behaves for tasks assigned to it. Standard is normal mouse/keyboard + tab-scoped detection. Dialer-exempt (e.g. Cold Calling, Sales) holds off idle while the agent is on a recognized dialer/CRM domain, same as before. Bounded grace (e.g. Backoffice) tolerates a set number of minutes of system idle — for work like downloading a call recording, uploading it, and editing it in a desktop spreadsheet app the extension can't see — before counting as idle like anyone else.

Tasks

Dialer / CRM domains

Users on these domains (or any subdomain of them) count as tracking, not idle, even with no mouse/keyboard activity — for softphone/dialer tools where they're on a call rather than typing. Changes here take effect for users within a few minutes, with no extension update or reload needed.

Extension version

After rolling out a new build to agents, raise this to that version to force everyone still on an older one off it — a below-minimum extension is blocked from starting new sessions, and an already-running session is stopped automatically within a minute. Leave blank (or set to 0.0.0) to allow any version.

Activity scoring ceilings

The activity % shown per agent and stored on every sample is mouse/keyboard event counts scored against these per-minute ceilings (100% = at or above the ceiling). The defaults (90 mouse, 60 keyboard) are starting guesses, not measured — pull a range of real activity_samples for your team (Reports tab, or query the table directly) and set these to what real, focused work actually looks like for your agents' roles. Leave either blank to use the extension's built-in default for that channel. Takes up to 5 minutes to apply to already-running sessions (cached client-side).

Add a user type

A user type controls which dashboard tabs an account can see, whether it can edit or only view each of those tabs, and — separately — which users' data it's allowed to see at all. Owner and Admin are protected and can't be edited or deleted here — both always see and edit everything. Creating, editing, resetting passwords for, or deleting user accounts on the Dashboard tab is always Owner/Admin only — no custom user type can be given that ability; custom user types can still be given view access to the Dashboard tab to see the team list. The User Management tab (this one) additionally breaks down into sections below — a user type can be given, say, Tasks but not User Types itself.
Check a tab to make it visible. For tabs with an "Edit" option, leave it unchecked to give this role read-only access to that tab.
Restricts the task dropdown in the extension to only these categories — e.g. a "Backoffice" user type only ever sees Backoffice tasks. Leave nothing checked for no restriction (this role sees every task, same as before). Owner/Admin are never restricted.
Restricts every tab above to just these users' data (Dashboard, Timesheets, Reports, Leads, Flags). Owner and Admin always see everyone regardless of this setting. Check as many of the first three as you like — they combine (e.g. "Only themselves" + "A specific user type" together). "All users" is exclusive since it already includes everyone.

ReadyMode

ReadyMode's Integrations team confirmed their API is lead-oriented only — Call Logs, Research Calls, and Agent/Productivity data isn't available via API. Two ways to get it in here instead: (1) automatically, via a ReadyMode Automated Task that emails a CSV on a schedule — see "Automated email imports" below; or (2) manually, by downloading a CSV from ReadyMode's Reports screen and pasting it into the boxes below. Note: ReadyMode's Productivity Report itself has no export option — use the Agent Report instead, which covers the same ground (Ready/Break time, calls made, etc.).

Agent → ReadyMode mapping

Match each Agent user to their ReadyMode username so their calls, research lookups, and productivity stats are attributed to them.

Voice calling (WebRTC)

The 📞 call button in chat connects two agents' browsers directly (peer-to-peer), using free public STUN servers by default — this works for most home/office networks but can fail to connect on stricter ones (some corporate firewalls, certain mobile carriers). If calls start failing to connect for some agents, add a TURN relay server.

Using Cloudflare? Cloudflare's TURN Token ID and API Token are NOT static credentials — don't paste them into the fields below (that won't work, and would expose a secret that can mint unlimited credentials). Instead, set them as secrets on the cloudflare-turn-credentials Supabase function (supabase secrets set CF_TURN_TOKEN_ID=... CF_TURN_API_TOKEN=...) and deploy it — calls will then auto-fetch short-lived TURN credentials with no fields to fill in here.

The fields below are for a different kind of TURN server: one that gives you a real static username/password (a self-hosted coturn, or another provider that issues long-lived credentials). They're only used as a fallback if the Cloudflare function above isn't set up. Leave blank to keep using STUN only (and Cloudflare, once configured). Both people still need dashboard.html open in a browser tab to call or receive a call — there's no ringing when the app is closed.

Client Chat Routing

Clients get an AI assistant in their portal's chat button. It answers simple questions itself, and routes anything else — or an explicit "Connect me to..." request — to whichever team below matches. Every staff member assigned to that team is notified and can see the conversation waiting in their own "Client Chats" panel — whoever clicks Accept first gets it assigned to them.

How this works

Each campaign below is built automatically from that campaign's own Client Qualification Form submission (Campaigns tab) — Name/Phone/Email are excluded, only the actual criteria answers are used. When a lead is submitted under a matching Campaign Name, Leads Queue Review's Campaign Fit tool evaluates it against this guide — a direct matching field on the lead's own form if one exists, otherwise a learned keyword association from past manually-reviewed leads on this same campaign — and rates it Strong Fit, Partial Fit, or Not a Fit. Opening Review there shows every criterion with an editable Meets/Doesn't Meet/Unclear rating; whatever a reviewer confirms or corrects is saved and used to improve future auto-ratings on that same campaign. A campaign with no Client Qualification Form submission yet, or a lead with nothing evaluable at all, shows no badge — nothing to rate it against yet.

One-time client charges

Charge a specific client a one-time amount (e.g. a setup fee) via Stripe. By default nothing is charged until the client pays it themselves from their own Billing tab or you send them a payment link — or use Charge now on a pending row below to debit their saved payment method directly. If a direct charge fails (declined card, no payment method on file, etc.), the reason is shown in the Status column so you know exactly why. Once a charge is paid, Partial refund in that same column issues a full or partial refund straight through Stripe, however it was originally paid.

Monthly campaign pricing used at checkout and for add-on changes (caller tiers, dialer, data).
